action_items: No functional fixes required. Every PRD acceptance item for Planning (projectreserveringen + leveranciersbestellingen) is verified end-to-end both at API and UI layer, with proper RBAC and stock semantics.
Optional cleanup (non-blocking, carried from iteration 2/3): migrate deprecated RN Web shadow* props to boxShadow and props.pointerEvents to style.pointerEvents.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py create_project (lines 1187-1223) does pre-flight availability check against physical_stock - reserved_stock BEFORE reserving. Reserve loop still uses atomic reserve_stock per line (reserve_line) so cross-request concurrency is still race-free; the pre-check only guards nicer error messages. The rollback branch after HTTPException properly deletes partial reservations, decrements reserved_stock, deletes events and the project — good atomic rollback (verified by test_line_over_available_409_and_nothing_created).

server.py reserve_line (line 1087) explicitly prevents duplicate active reservation on same project+article via early find_one; also catches DuplicateKeyError on client_request_id as the idempotent path returning the SAME reservation. Correct.

server.py build_order_lines (1370-1393) validates: no duplicate article in lines (422), article change on a line with received>0 blocked (409), ordered<received blocked (409) and prevents deleting a received line. Covered by test_lower_ordered_below_received_409.

server.py receive_order (1475-1523) uses supplier_receipts collection with unique index on client_request_id for cross-request idempotency, and $elemMatch guard {ordered, received <= ordered - qty} with $inc on both line.received and version to atomically increment. Rollback branch reverses the $inc if the subsequent book_mutation call fails. Clean.

server.py update_order (1441-1472) uses two-way optimistic lock: compares data.version==o.version AND uses find_one_and_update with {_id, version: o.version} + $inc version. Correct — produces 409 on stale (test_stale_version_409).
server.py list_orders status filter supports 'open' (besteld+gedeeltelijk) / 'volledig_ontvangen' / 'alle', but the frontend segment chip is labeled 'Openstaand' -> 'open' which matches.
Frontend bestelling/[id].tsx (line 206) uses order-receive-confirm testID with dynamic title '{total} stuks binnenboeken'; disabled when total==0 — good UX guard.

Frontend planning.tsx (line 58): single 'planning-new-project' or 'planning-new-order' testID is swapped based on view — tests should toggle segment first before asserting presence. Not a bug, just a note.
